extracted.intended_audience: BBC content-makers, producers, editors and commissioning staff
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial guidance for BBC output on avoiding harm and unjustifiable offence, including principles, scheduling rules and mandatory referral requirements for potentially harmful or offensive material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance freedom of expression with avoiding unjustifiable offence
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC aims to reflect the world as it is ... The BBC must balance its right to freedom of expression, which allows it to publish innovative and challenging content, with the responsibility of avoiding unjustifiable offence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Freedom of expression includes audience rights to access creative material, information, ideas and contentious or offensive content but is subject to restrictions prescribed by law and necessary in a democratic society. Editorial decisions should weigh the value of expression against potential unjustifiable offence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportionate care for creative risk-taking
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative risk-taking is a vital part of the BBC's mission. However, in all output, the greater the risk of causing harm or offence, the greater the thought, care and planning required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher-risk material requires stronger editorial justification, additional planning and safeguards. Do not treat creative risk as a carte blanche to publish distressing material without commensurate editorial process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of child and young person for these Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purposes of the Editorial Guidelines and unless stated otherwise, a child is someone under the age of 16 years. Young people are those aged 16 and 17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are editorial (not legal) definitions and set a higher standard than Ofcom in some respects. Apply protections for under-16s accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect audiences from offensive/harmful material unless sufficient editorial purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC must protect audiences from offensive and harmful material unless it has sufficient editorial purpose. Content that is potentially highly offensive will need the strongest editorial justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where editorial purpose is claimed, ensure the purpose is explicit and documented; content lacking clear editorial justification should be avoided or altered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take account of 'generally accepted standards' and audience expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Content makers should take account of 'generally accepted standards' as well as audience expectations when considering publishing potentially offensive or harmful material. The publication or broadcast of such content must be justified by the context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Potentially offensive content includes strong language, violence, sex, sexual violence, humiliation, distress, violation of human dignity, and discriminatory treatment or language. Evaluate context, likely audience, and prevailing social standards before publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear content information for audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Audiences must have clear information to allow them to assess whether content will be suitable for them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use content warnings, signposting, ratings, labelling and scheduling information so audiences can make informed choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong language requires editorial justification and signposting
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of strong language must be editorially justified and appropriately signposted to ensure it meets audience expectations, wherever it appears.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong language should be flagged in advance and only used where it serves a clear editorial purpose. Consider frequency, context and audience when deciding to include it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect children and young people from material that may impair development
rubrics_metrics.description: Material that might seriously impair the physical, mental or moral development of children and young people must not be broadcast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Err on the side of protecting under-16s; do not broadcast material likely to seriously harm development. Consider edits, scheduling, labelling or exclusion when in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance child protection with children's rights to expression and information
rubrics_metrics.description: The responsibility to protect children and young people from potentially harmful or offensive content must be balanced with their rights to freedom of expression and freedom to receive information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess both protection and rights; for user-generated contributions by young people, apply special safeguards described elsewhere in the Guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate scheduling and labelling for material unsuitable for children
rubrics_metrics.description: Material that might be unsuitable for children must be appropriately scheduled – in television, observing the 9pm watershed and, in radio, having regard to times when children are particularly likely to be listening. Online material must be suitably placed and labelled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmes should be pre-watershed compliant if broadcast before 9pm; online placement and labelling must allow parents/guardians to make informed choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory referrals must be made in advance
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandatory referrals must be referred in advance. Mandatory referrals are an essential part of the BBC's editorial and compliance process and must be observed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the referral process as non-optional. Seek advice from named senior editorial figures or Director Editorial Policy and Standards where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral for proposals showing the real moment of someone's death
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to show the real moment of someone's death must be referred to Director Editorial Policy and Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such material requires highest-level consideration; consult section 5.4.37 for further detail and expected justification/safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral for depictions of the Prophet Muhammad
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to publish or broadcast a depiction of the Prophet Muhammad must be referred to a senior editorial figure who must consult Director Editorial Policy and Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a specially sensitive religious referral; follow the prescribed escalation and consult 5.4.67 for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-watershed suitability for UK TV between 5.30am and 9pm
rubrics_metrics.description: Programmes broadcast on UK television between 5.30am and 9pm must be suitable for a general audience which might include children. Only in exceptional circumstances can there be any departure from this practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any exceptions must be referred to the person running the channel and clear content information should be given. Programmes that straddle the watershed should normally be pre-watershed compliant throughout; consult Editorial Policy for exceptions (see 5.4.11 and 5.4.12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral for use of the strongest language (explicit words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to use the strongest language (cunt, motherfucker or fuck and its derivatives) must be referred to and approved by the relevant head of channel, who should consider the editorial justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial Policy may also be consulted. Use of these words is exceptional and requires explicit approval and recorded justification (see 5.4.31).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval required for use of strongest racist language
rubrics_metrics.description: The divisional director, or their named delegate, must approve the use of the strongest racist language, as listed in Ofcom's 'strong' column, in any upcoming programmes or output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such language requires senior-level sign-off; see 5.4.24 and 5.4.33 for context and handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral for graphic scenes of animal cruelty or apparent mistreatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to include graphic scenes of animal cruelty or apparent mistreatment must be referred to a senior editorial figure or, for independent production companies, to the commissioning editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graphic animal cruelty requires strong editorial justification even if recorded in countries where it is legal. Consider alternatives, warnings, and contextual necessity (see 5.4.42).

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral for portrayal of hanging, suicide, attempted suicide or self-harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to include a hanging scene, portray suicide, attempted suicide or self-harm requires careful consideration because of the sensitivity of the subject and the possibility of imitation and must be referred to a senior editorial figure or, for independent production companies, to the commissioning editor. Referral must also be made to Editorial Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High sensitivity due to risk of imitation; require specialist review, mitigation (e.g., helplines), and strong editorial justification (see 5.4.58).

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral for demonstrations of hypnosis
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to feature a demonstration of hypnosis must be referred to a senior editorial figure or, for independent production companies, to the commissioning editor, who must consult Editorial Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hypnosis demonstrations may pose safety/ethical issues; consult Editorial Policy (see 5.4.69) and consider expert input or avoidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval for flashing images or strobing sequences that fail technical checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to include flashing images or strobing sequences in recorded programmes which fail the Transmission Review technical checks must be approved by the relevant output controller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect audience health (e.g., epilepsy triggers). If technical checks fail, do not broadcast without output-controller approval (see 5.4.72).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition and referral regarding subliminal or non-aware influence techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Any techniques which exploit the possibility of conveying a message to audiences or otherwise influencing their minds, without their being aware, or fully aware, of what has occurred must not be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such techniques may include subliminal messages and images of very brief duration. Anyone who has reason to believe their content might contain such a technique must refer to a senior editorial figure or, for independent production companies, to the commissioning editor, who should consult Editorial Policy (see 5.4.73).
